part: in-house guard machinery: about 18 plugins and hook sets, with a separate blocking hook on ten or more cards
problem: Built as written, the 42 cards ask Tony to write and look after about 18 in-house plugins, hook sets and wrappers, seven new agents, about 15 host scripts and 30 or more recurring jobs, for two adults; the config repo holds one plugin today. Ten or more cards bring a blocking hook of their own, three separate plugins sit on the same outgoing text, and nine cards then carry a paragraph on how those collide.
checked: Re-counted the 'how' fields of r7.json: 12 cards name a before_tool_call handler (two reuse G009's), 7 a phrase matcher, 3 a message_sending cancel, 10 an in-house plugin or tool, 9 a host command job; new agents are research, family-group, two mail readers, home, desk and kids. ~/src/happy-config/plugins holds only home-weather. Roadmap lines 113, 147 and 418: the roadmap itself asks for hooks that fail closed, as one registry plugin that pins recipients and checks which agent may call which account server; it asks for no cap, stop, journal or gate plugin. Installed docs plugins/hooks/reference.md:93: a blocking handler that throws blocks the call, so every extra plugin is one more thing that can stop every tool.

proposal.text: One small 'house rules' plugin, which is the roadmap's own shape, with one blocking handler and a short rule table. A rule is added only when a picked feature needs it: first the reminder target (F007), then the memory write path (F041), then a family-only recipient if cross-parent texts are ever switched on. State a budget in the summary: the first slice adds no plugin, the second step adds this one. Condition for 'no plugin' while mail is in the first slice: the mail connector is allowed on the mail agent only and denied by name on every other agent, the separation check and the 'read the other parent's mail' canary are extended to it, and the roadmap's test that an agent sees exactly one account server is run before go-live. Quiet hours come from the time in each job's schedule line. The other cards keep their guard designs as notes, not commitments.

loses: Per-card independence of the guards, the daily cap and mute by chat (see G001), and, until the plugin exists, the roadmap's second layer on account servers (its code check in section 1b): for the first slice, separation rests on tool policy, the explicit deny and the tests.
challenge_note: Merged the total-machinery row with the one-hook-per-card row; the roadmap requires fail-closed hooks only as one registry plugin (lines 113 and 147), so the finding stands, and I added the conditions under which mail can go live before that plugin exists and said what is given up meanwhile.

challenge_note: Neither the roadmap nor any answer of Tony's requires the gate, and it guards only against a parent's own slip with one file type; I kept the audio-off switch and the hand-off test in the simpler design because the card's safety text depends on them.

part: in-house stop plugin as Jordan's substitute for the command list
problem: Tony said there was 'no need' to add Jordan to the command list. The summary took that to mean she needs another way to stop Happy and files a plugin with four hooks, a kill file and a lock-out phrase under 'decided'; he may have meant she needs no stop at all.
checked: owner-facts.md ('No need'); frame.findings[2] and frame.decisions[2] and [10]; G005 how and its eight caveats (the built-in stop ends one answer and pauses no job; the plugin stops model-free jobs only on a best-effort basis); dependants CRT-13 (its fixed emergency reply shares the plugin's hook), CRT-05 (an optional pause step) and MAC-02 (parked); roadmap line 141 (the control plane is Tony's alone; family members only chat); CRT-05 how (after a shutdown the Mac waits at the disk-unlock screen).

proposal.text: Does Jordan need a way to stop Happy by text? Default: no. Then G005 is one printed sheet of the built-in commands for you and the plugin is not built. Jordan's stop goes on the recovery card: shut the Mac mini down; it stays off until someone unlocks it. Your own stop-everything stays the scheduler switch and stopping the gateway. If yes: compare the one config line you declined (it gives her 'stop' for one answer and the status commands, not a stop-everything) with the plugin before building either.

loses: A stop-everything by one text for either parent, Tony included, and the lost-phone lock-out by text (Tony removes the handle and redeploys instead). CRT-13's fixed emergency reply would need its own small matcher or go with it.
challenge_note: Nothing in the roadmap or the fact sheet asks for a second adult's stop, so the question stands; I added a no-software stop for Jordan (shutting the Mac down) and named the two cards that lean on the plugin.

part: notification policy plugin: daily cap, classes, mute and vacation mode
problem: Tony has never asked for quiet hours or a cap on texts, and the jobs it would limit do not exist yet. Because the plugin drops a held text and never sends it later, nine other cards carry workarounds for it.
checked: owner-facts.md 'Never stated' (quiet hours, a daily cap); G001 how and caveats 1, 2 and 12; the workaround caveats on G003, G005, CRT-04, F006, F014, F018, F063, CRT-13 and F076; depends_on of F018, F063, F076 and AUT-01, which need it only for the classes and windows it would itself impose; roadmap: no cap or quiet-hours rule anywhere.

proposal.text: No policy plugin. Each job gets a daytime hour in its schedule line and stays silent when it has nothing to say. A parent who wants fewer texts asks Tony to switch a job off, and each iPhone can already silence the night. Revisit only if the family reports too many texts.

loses: The daily cap, the urgent or not-urgent split, and 'mute until 3' or a holiday pause by chat.
challenge_note: Looked for a requirement in the roadmap, the fact sheet and the dependent cards and found none beyond what the plugin itself creates; it only restricts, so dropping it breaks no rule.

part: change journal, weekly review and undo
problem: A large build whose job is to record and reverse writes by tools that are not built yet. Every write tool has to log an inverse, saved notes are copied into the shared store and then need their own per-person filter and retention rule, and the card says most undo requests are just a second write.
checked: G006 how, caveats 5, 6, 9 and 11, effort (L) and depends_on (F031, F041, F030, F007, F010: none built); no card lists G006 as a prerequisite; F041 safety, which names the weekly review as the way to see what memory kept; owner-facts.md (Tony can read everyone's data); the first slice has no write tool to journal.

proposal.text: Park the card. 'What did you save about me?' is answered from that parent's own memory files, Tony can read those files and the built-in tool audit when needed, and forgetting a conversation stays the operator command it already is.

loses: The Sunday 'what Happy did' text and 'undo that'; the check on what memory kept becomes a question a parent asks or a look by Tony, not a weekly text.
challenge_note: No other card depends on it and nothing it would record exists yet; I stated the one real loss more fully, since the memory card names this review as its safeguard.

part: job generator and per-job charters in the first step
problem: A generator that creates, compares and removes jobs and renders a written charter per job sits in the first wave, where only two cards have operator-made jobs. The card itself says its three safety switches are plain config and that a charter is prompt text, not enforcement.
checked: G003 how and caveats 1, 4 and 8; wave A cards with operator-made jobs (G008 and CRT-04); value 5 in r7.index.md; roadmap line 142 (delivery targets are generated from the family file and never edited by hand) and line 150 (a job delivers only to its owner).

proposal.text: Now: the three scheduler switches, with failure alerts routed to Tony. Jobs: one short checked-in script that creates each job, with the owner's handle read from the family file and never typed in, a time limit and a tool list on every job, and the job's rules in its own message. The existing inspect check lists every job, disabled ones included. Build the generator, its comparison and the charters when the script holds more jobs than can be read at a glance.

loses: Per-person on and off switches in the family file, the parent-readable charter, and automatic clean-up of jobs that no longer match the file.
challenge_note: Repaired: the roadmap wants job targets to come from the family file (line 142), so the simpler script has to read handles from it; the comparing generator and the charters go beyond that rule and can wait.

part: household store with no first-step user; four places for family knowledge
problem: The shared database is in wave A, but nothing in wave A needs it except two optional steps; its users are later cards. With it the first wave has four places to keep what the family knows (each parent's notes, rendered facts, the shared handbook, the database).
checked: depends_on of every record that names F031 (wave A: G009's relay step and F043, both optional; later: G001, G006, CRT-10, CRT-13, F063, F014, F010, CRT-11, F033, F080, AUT-01); F031 caveat 1; F043 how and caveat 2 (that a sandboxed agent's memory search can read a shared folder is untested); descriptions of F041 and F042; roadmap: no shared database, and line 137 (shared agents keep no memory).

proposal.text: First steps keep two places for what the family knows: what Tony types into the family file (rendered by F042's one generator step) and each parent's own notes (F041). A shared handbook folder (F043 step 1, without the wiki plugin) joins only after its untested point passes. 'Filter every 90 days' is a repeating calendar event or reminder. Build the store when a picked feature needs dates worked out in code.

loses: Shared rows that either parent can update by chat, until then.
challenge_note: Checked every dependant: all are optional steps or cards that other rows park or simplify; I moved the shared folder behind its own untested point, which leaves two places instead of three.

part: cross-parent texts and the ask-and-relay step, and the value of 5
problem: The relay needs a table of open requests, a plugin that matches a bare yes or no and a timer for the reminder and expiry. The card itself calls this a small convenience, yet it is rated value 5 and re-opens the roadmap's rule against sending into other conversations, which lets one parent's agent put what it holds in front of the other parent.
checked: G009 how, caveat 1, safety, depends_on 2 and unverified 6 ('Judgement, not sourced'); roadmap line 150 (no sends into other conversations), line 147 and the S2 step (a send to another family member counts as a wrong recipient), line 493 (one data domain per person, By: You); openclaw.json line 169 (both switches off today); F007 depends_on 2, which needs the hook's check on the scheduling tool and not the cross-parent send; the other dependants are CRT-04's notice, CRT-10's tracked ask and cards parked in C, D or Later.

proposal.text: Drop the relay and leave both cross-conversation switches off, as the roadmap has them. The part timed reminders need (refuse a web address or any target but the asker on a reminder, and require an empty tool list) moves to F007 as the first rule of the one house-rules plugin. The item is not shown as value 5.

loses: Happy passing a note or a yes-or-no between the parents, and Happy's own notices reaching the other parent.
challenge_note: The simpler design is the roadmap's own rule and a By: You decision; the only part another early card needs is the scheduler check for F007, which I kept, and I raised the severity because the card relaxes a separation rule for what it calls a convenience.

part: outage notice script
problem: A host script would watch an alert, text both parents 'down' and later 'back', and check quiet hours itself. The card says a parent who texts during an outage already sees the failure, Tony already gets the alerts, and the fallback model is not recommended.
checked: CRT-04 how, caveats 7, 8 and 9, unverified 1 and depends_on (G008 and G009); frame.decisions[9] recommendation (b); roadmap O1 alert rules (line 447: model and gateway alerts already reach the operator by ntfy); no card depends on CRT-04.

proposal.text: Nothing to build. One line on the printed sheet, worded after one real error text has been seen: if Happy answers with an error, the model service is down; try again later. The fallback model stays off, as the summary already recommends.

loses: An unprompted 'model is down' and 'back' text to both parents.
challenge_note: No rule or dependant needs the script, and it relies on cross-parent delivery that the roadmap keeps off; the sheet line waits for one real error text because the card has not seen its wording.

part: a wave A card that exists only to gate two parked cards
problem: The deny list guards against a paired Mac or phone, but nothing is paired, pairing has been manual-only since M0, and its only dependants are two value-2 cards in wave D and Later. The card says the family sees no change.
checked: MAC-04 description, how and caveats 1 and 4; ~/src/happy-config/openclaw/openclaw.json line 23 (automatic and SSH-verified pairing both off); depends_on of OCL-01 and MAC-02; installed docs nodes/computer-use.md:220 (an operator who wants screen control off can deny the command with one config line).

proposal.text: Not a first-wave item: it becomes step 1 of whichever of OCL-01 or MAC-02 is ever picked. If Tony wants cover in case he tries the Mac or iPhone app outside the catalog, the one documented deny line for screen control can ride along in any ordinary deploy; the phone-command list, the extra posture-check lines and the off-switch notes wait.

loses: A written limit in config ahead of time; a device paired by mistake before then is covered only if the one line is added.
challenge_note: Narrowed: the installed guide does offer the deny line and it costs one line of config, so it may ride along; nothing requires the card's full list before a device is paired.

part: skills pipeline before there is a routine to teach
problem: To teach a routine the card adds a file-read grant on the parents' agents, a deploy step for skill folders and a proof that the memory hook refuses writes there. The card itself says a routine of a few lines can live in the agent's instruction file, which works today, and no parent has described a routine yet.
checked: AUT-06 how, depends_on 1, 4 and 5 and caveats 6 and 9; frame.decisions[8] options (a) and (b); roadmap lines 126 and 492 (skills inside each agent, By: You): the roadmap chose skills over extra agents, not a skills pipeline now; templates/person/AGENTS.md exists in the config repo; G003 caveat 2 (that file has a size budget).

proposal.text: Take option (b) for now: a routine is a few reviewed lines in the agent's instruction file, deployed as today, with no file-read grant and no skills step. Skills stay the roadmap's home for know-how and come back when there are more routines than fit in that file. Nothing is built until a parent describes a first routine.

loses: Routines loaded only when needed, and the practice quiz as a named skill.
challenge_note: The roadmap's By: You choice is skills as the place for know-how, which instruction-file lines respect, so this is a deferral and not a reversal; option (b) is also the tighter one because it adds no file-read grant.

part: generated dates table, monthly script and lead-time rules
problem: A table generated from the family file, a script with lead-time rules, a monthly job per parent and a workaround for the text cap, all for a handful of dates a year. Nobody has said which passports, cars or domains exist.
checked: F063 how, caveats 1, 2 and 6 and depends_on; owner-facts.md 'Never stated' (cars, passports, insurance); dependants F028 (parked) and CRT-13 (uses only the table's document dates).

proposal.text: Each expiry or upkeep date is one calendar event with an alert, typed once on the family's own calendar, which also works when Happy is down; or a dated reminder from Happy once F007 exists. The lead time is chosen when it is typed. No table, script or monthly job.

loses: One combined monthly look-ahead text, and upkeep intervals that restart by chat.
challenge_note: No rule or early card needs the table; I put a plain calendar event first because it needs no build and does not depend on Happy being up.

part: five watcher scripts with keyword lists and state files
problem: Five host scripts (storm alerts, team schedules, page changes, two recall feeds), each with state files and keyword lists. The card says none gives earlier notice than the source's own service: the phone's weather alerts, the team app and the recall agencies' own sign-ups.
checked: F018 how, effort (L) and caveat 2; plugins/home-weather/nws.js in the config repo, which already fetches active alerts with every forecast; owner-facts.md (no teams, allergies or owned-item lists recorded); the only dependant is CRT-11 (parked).

proposal.text: No watcher scripts in the first build. Happy's weather answers already carry active alerts for home, and each parent can switch on the phone's own severe-weather notifications. A storm text is built only if Tony asks for one on top of that; recall, page and schedule watches wait until someone names a page worth watching.

loses: A text from Happy at the moment an alert is issued, recall matching against family lists and moved-game texts.
challenge_note: Confirmed in the weather plugin's code that alerts already come with every forecast, and no live card needs the scripts; the default is now no script at all, which matches the verdict reached in this card's own part of the review.

part: three briefs per parent with driver tags and a gear table
problem: Six scheduled jobs for two people, a rule that parents tag each calendar event with who drives, and a routines-and-gear table in the agent's instructions. None of the routines, the tag habit or the three times comes from Tony, and the calendar it reads is not chosen yet.
checked: F014 how and caveats 1, 2, 4 and 7; owner-facts.md 'Never stated' (calendar, routines, times); F009 depends_on 1 (Google or iCloud still open); roadmap lines 121 and 278: the only scheduled text it plans is the 07:00 mail digest; value 5 in r7.index.md.

proposal.text: One evening text for Tony: tomorrow's calendar and the weather, silent when nothing is on, at a time he sets. It waits for the calendar answer. The week-ahead, the morning brief, driver lines and the gear table are added only when asked.

loses: The Sunday week-ahead, the morning brief and who-drives lines at first.
challenge_note: No roadmap line, source or dependent card needs three briefs or the tag; the proposal matches the verdict in this card's own part of the review and I made it wait for the calendar answer.

part: dose-log tool, 14-day sweep and phrase matcher
problem: An in-house tool, a deletion sweep and a phrase matcher to answer 'when was the last dose?'. The card's own source says the log should stay with the medicine, and the card says a shared note on the parents' phones already does this, works when Happy is down and keeps a child's health notes off the cloud model.
checked: CRT-10 how and caveats 3, 4, 5 and 7; its 'Backed by' source as summarised on the card; depends_on (F031, F007, F009, G009's relay step); no card depends on CRT-10; owner-facts.md (medications never stated).

proposal.text: No build. If asked, Happy suggests a shared note kept with the medicine and never advises a dose.

loses: Elapsed time worked out in code, and the sick-day add-ons.
challenge_note: The card's own source and caveats argue for the shared note, nothing depends on the tool, and dropping it keeps a child's health notes out of three places the card says its deletion cannot reach.

part: three bundles in one card; only the sign-in expiry check has a user
problem: The card bundles a daily health script, a scheduled security audit with change comparison, monthly and quarterly checklist texts and extra eval cases. It says itself that gateway-down and iMessage alerts already exist and that the monthly part is 'checklist lines and not a feature'.
checked: G008 how and caveats 1, 2 and 5; roadmap O0 and O1 (lines 445 to 447), line 433 (monthly audit, quarterly restore drill and key rotation) and line 510 (audit after every update): the roadmap asks for these checks, not for a scheduled job that runs and compares them; owner-facts.md (evals on demand, never on a schedule).

proposal.text: Keep one thing, added with the mail slice: a daily check that the Google sign-in is still valid, because an expired sign-in would otherwise show up only as a missing or empty digest. The monthly and quarterly checklists become calendar reminders for Tony, the audit stays a command he runs after each update and monthly as the roadmap says, and behaviour test cases join the existing eval suite when a feature that needs them lands.

loses: Automatic comparison of audit results between runs, and a text when a plugin fails to load.
challenge_note: Narrowed: the roadmap does require the audit and the drills (lines 433 and 510), so they stay as Tony's own cadence; only the scheduling, the comparison and the texts go beyond it.

part: that a reminder can be created from an iMessage turn
problem: The headline reminder feature rests on a step nobody has tried: the card says creating a reminder from an iMessage turn 'has not been tried live'. Its prerequisites still name adding Jordan as an owner as the decision, after Tony's 'no need'.
checked: F007 unverified 1, depends_on 1 and 3, and safety; installed docs automation/cron-jobs/managing-jobs.md, 'Conversational management' (a listed channel owner may list, inspect, update, run or remove jobs; creating through chat is stated for Control UI administrators) and automation/cron-jobs/how-it-works.md lines 61 to 66 (an agent that holds the automations tool offers to create a routine after a confirmation): the two pages do not settle an iMessage turn; owner-facts.md ('No need').

proposal.text: With script triggers switched off first, one live try by Tony: a throwaway reminder set from iMessage on an agent that holds no memory, checked for creation, firing time and that it reaches only him. Do this before the hook rule is designed. Build for Tony only, and ask once whether 'no need' also covers making Jordan a command owner (default: yes, it does).

loses: nothing
challenge_note: Read both installed pages: neither states that a channel owner's chat turn can create a job, so the test is needed; I added that the trigger switch goes off before the try, as the card's own safety text requires.

part: 'ready now' and the family facts it says it renders
problem: The card is marked ready now and says both agents will start every chat knowing the kids' school, routines and activities and the language to reply in. The family file holds none of those facts, the generator has no step that renders them, and Tony never mentioned a second language or grandparents.
checked: scripts/gen-family.mjs in the config repo (263 lines: it copies four template files into each person's workspace and renders no facts, preferences or language); owner-facts.md (the family file holds two adults, a home town and a point; a second language and grandparents never stated); F042 caveat 8 (the generator and registry 'were not opened in this review').

proposal.text: Readiness 'needs a build', not 'ready now'. Describe it as: Tony types the facts he wants known into the family file, and the generator gains one step to render them. Drop the reply-language and grandparent lines unless Tony confirms them.

loses: nothing
challenge_note: Opened the generator the card says it did not open: it renders no facts, so 'ready now' is unbacked and the readiness label should change with the wording.

part: that the family wants lights and speakers controlled
problem: The Hue bridge and Sonos speakers are known only from a network scan; Tony has not said he wants them controlled. The summary's decision asks which route to build, not whether.
checked: owner-facts.md 'Known from a scan, not from Tony', and Tony's own examples of advanced abilities (a computer, an idle iPhone), which do not include the house; frame.decisions[6]; F076 effort (L) and wave (C).

proposal.text: Do you want Happy to switch lights or speakers at all? Default: no; F076 is parked and its decision leaves the list.

loses: Nothing unless he says yes.
challenge_note: The fact sheet lists the devices as seen in a scan and not as a wish, and no roadmap milestone covers house devices, so the question stands as written.
